review_candidates.title: Climate Mitigation Data Engineer: Building Climate Solutions for Cities
review_candidates.description: Climate Mitigation Data Engineer :  Building Climate Solutions for Cities Link to application: https://noteforms.com/forms/climate-data-engineer-job-application-cihkkr Have you built a solid career in data engineering and now want your work to actually matter? Open Earth Foundation is a California-based nonprofit on a mission to create groundbreaking technology that helps combat the climate crisis. Our climate platforms support cities around the world with data-driven climate planning and delivery. We’re a diverse, global team working remotely and collaborating with partners worldwide to make real change possible. With strong funding and a powerhouse team of innovators, we’re ready to tackle big challenges for a resilient Earth for generations to come and we need the planet’s brightest minds to help solve them! Your mission, should you choose to accept it: As a Climate Mitigation Data Engineer at Open Earth Foundation, you build the data cities use to plan, act on and track their climate goals. That starts with greenhouse-gas inventories cities can trust, and runs through estimating what each action could cut, to monitoring progress and reporting it. Cities need to know where their emissions come from, report them to frameworks such as the GHG Protocol for Cities (GPC) and CDP, and track progress over time. You own that mitigation record: the methods, the inputs, and the models behind the numbers. A Data Platform Engineer owns the shared warehouse and the pipeline platform. You decide whether a calculation is right, which dataset it should use, and where the gaps are. Together you put that domain on a platform other Digital Service applications can use. Colleagues on the data team cover climate risk and adaptation. This role is focused on mitigation. This is a mid-level role. You ship datasets and reviewed methods with your manager. You are not expected to design the warehouse architecture. This position is fully remote and international as our organization works across different time zones. Schedule flexibility is expected with a willingness to collaborate in overlapping core hours for meetings from 8am PST to 11am PST (GMT-8). Availability to work with overlapping hours across U.S., Latin American and European time zones is preferred. Experience with asynchronous remote work and the ability to self-organize tasks is preferred. Priority will be given to applications submitted by November 15th.   The following requirements describe our ideal candidate. If you don't meet some of the requirements, you're encouraged to apply anyway. Let us know if there is something missing and how we can work together to make it up. Essential Functions and Specific Duties:  Design and maintain the data models for emissions inventories, activity data, emission factors, sources, and methodologies Build and run pipelines that ingest national, global, and city-provided datasets into those models, with tests, versioning, and clear lineage Review technical methodologies for emissions calculations: check the logic, data inputs, assumptions, and global-warming-potential choices, and flag gaps Encode reporting rules so outputs align with the GPC and with other frameworks cities submit to, including CDP where relevant Snapshot factors and methods onto results so a historical inventory stays reproducible when a catalogue changes later Set data-quality checks and compare results against independent sources Document data models, pipelines, and methods so partners and colleagues can follow how every number was produced Work with the Systems Data Engineer so domain models land in the shared warehouse as contracts, not as a private schema Support cities and partners with emissions profiles and with questions about where a number came from Use AI tools for dataset discovery, cleaning, documentation, and method review, and check the output before it is used   Other: Actively participate in team building and culture development activities at Open Earth Foundation Qualifications:  5+ years in data engineering or a closely related role Strong Python and SQL Working knowledge of greenhouse-gas accounting frameworks, such as the GHG Protocol for Cities (GPC) or IPCC methods Solid understanding of relational databases and schema design (for example PostgreSQL) Experience with at least one pipeline or orchestration tool (for example dbt, Airflow, Dagster, Mage, or similar) Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and data warehouses (for example BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, or PostgreSQL used as an analytical store) Nice to have Hands-on experience building or reviewing city or national emissions inventories Emission-factor catalogues, notation keys (IE, NE, NO, C), and data-quality tiers Familiarity with GPC sectors, scopes, and BASIC / BASIC+ reporting levels CDP, Common Reporting Format, or eCRF reporting Geospatial data and tools (PostGIS, GeoPandas) for allocating activity data to cities Hands-on use of AI tools or LLMs in data workflows A MSc or PhD in Environmental Science, Climate Science, Environmental Engineering, Data Science, or a related field is highly desirable, particularly with research experience in greenhouse-gas accounting, emissions modeling, or climate data systems. Interpersonal Skills: Explains technical methods in plain language to non-technical colleagues, cities, and partners Works well with external partners such as research institutions and climate networks, including C40, the Global Covenant of Mayors, and CDP Collaborates closely with the Systems Data Engineer, and with full-stack, AI, design, and product teams, helping shape how emissions data shows up in products Comfortable saying when a number is not ready to publish, and what would make it ready Compensation and Benefits:   This position is full-time with compensation of $55,000 to $70,000 /year (USD) , dependent on experience and location Open Earth offers unlimited paid time off, paid holidays and paid sick leave You will work remotely within a dynamic and international environment  We celebrate our achievements during our annual team retreat OEF is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, age, religion, national origin, or any other protected characteristic. We celebrate diversity, equity, and inclusion in our teams and believe people should align their work with their purpose. Join us if you love Earth. We look forward to hearing from you! review_candidates.title: Senior Backend Engineer
review_candidates.description: The Role At Modaxo, we're passionate about changing the face of people transportation. We believe that all transportation services should be safe, efficient, convenient, and equitable. Our products power mission-critical operations across a variety of industry sectors. We're making a strategic investment in AI to transform our solutions. You will build the core services of a new enterprise AI platform - the APIs, orchestration, and data and integration on-ramps that our products build on. We ship working software on aggressive timelines; perfect is the enemy of shipped. You'll report to the Head of AI Platform Engineering and join a small, senior founding team building the platform from the ground up. The opportunity: build the services an entire product portfolio depends on, with a clean slate and real ownership. Why this role is different It's platform AND product. You build reusable platform capability while enabling product teams to ship features fast - balancing leverage with velocity. It's domain-first, not tech-first. You'll learn our customers' operational domain; the best platform choices come from understanding how the work actually runs. It's pragmatic build/buy. We win on integration and reliability using proven components - pragmatic decisions, not gold-plating. It's a founding role - you help build the team. As an early hire you'll set the patterns, tests, and guardrails others build on, and help raise the bar as we hire. It's production-first, not research-first. We ship on aggressive timelines and own what we ship. It's value-based. You'll validate with product teams and customers and prioritize by value - building what moves outcomes, not what's novel. What You'll Do Core Platform Services Design and build core backend services - APIs, orchestration, and access control - as reliable, well-tested production systems. Shape API design and developer experience for internal and external consumers of the platform. Contribute to the reference architecture and design records; keep boundaries clean so components stay swappable. Multi-Tenant SaaS & Integration Build for multiple customers on shared infrastructure: isolation, quotas, and usage metering done properly. Build data and integration on-ramps - connector frameworks and governed data access that are idempotent and reliable at scale. Ownership & Reliability Own services end to end: design, implementation, tests, deployment, and on-call for what you ship. Model failure modes explicitly - partial failure, retries, consistency, back-pressure - and design for them. Delivering Value with Product & Customers Work with product teams and customers to validate results and outcomes, prioritizing by value. Take a value-based development approach: prove value with the smallest useful slice, then scale what works. Instrument and measure impact; let evidence - not opinion - drive what ships. Build automated QA - tests, quality gates, and regression checks - into the delivery pipeline. Building the Team & Ways of Working Help build the team: contribute to hiring, raise the bar in interviews, and mentor as we grow. Foster a culture of technical excellence, customer obsession, and pragmatic shipping. Partner with product teams across the portfolio who own their own roadmaps. What You'll Bring We look at demonstrated experience and scope, not years served - and we don't expect every candidate to tick every box. Production distributed systems: You've built and operated production backend or distributed services that other teams depend on. End-to-end ownership: You own correctness, tests, and operations for what you build. Trade-off reasoning: You describe systems by the trade-offs you made, not just the technologies you used. Clear communication: You explain your thinking clearly to engineers, product partners, and customers, and bring people along. Value and pragmatism: You focus on outcomes and value and make pragmatic calls to ship. Bonus Points Any of these strengthen an application - none are required: Multi-tenant SaaS: Backend services serving many customers with enforced isolation and metering. Gateways & orchestration: API gateways or workflow orchestration at scale. Integration frameworks: Connector or integration frameworks (API/EDI/CDC), not one-off scripts. LLM-backed services: Backend work behind AI or LLM features in production. Languages: Strength in C#/.NET or Python; Go a bonus. Architecture experience: System/platform design and trade-off judgement - one-way vs two-way doors. Enterprise scale: Experience building or operating enterprise-scale software and its reliability, security, and integration demands. AI-assisted engineering: You use AI coding assistants productively and supervise their output with judgement. New to some of this? If you bring the essentials above and are excited by the problem, we'd still like to hear from you.
